name: Predetermined Change Control Plans
blurb: Getting FDA approval in advance for planned model updates.
title: Predetermined Change Control Plans
answer: A predetermined change control plan describes the model changes a maker intends to make after authorization, how each will be developed and validated, and how its impact will be assessed. Once authorized with the device, those changes can ship without a new submission. The FDA's December 2024 final guidance applies to all AI enabled device software, and labels must say the device uses machine learning and has an authorized plan.

reading.body:
A predetermined change control plan lets an approved medical AI device ship planned model updates without a new FDA submission.

The mechanism is a pre-approval of change itself. A maker writes down which model changes it intends to make after authorization, how each will be developed and validated, and how its impact will be assessed. Once the device is authorized with that plan, those changes can ship without a new submission. The FDA finalized this guidance in December 2024, and it applies to all AI enabled device software. Labels must state that the device uses machine learning and has an authorized plan.

For medtech teams the practical consequence is timing. The change plan belongs in the first submission, not in a later amendment. Retraining on new data and expanding to new populations are named as the changes most worth pre-authorizing, which is another way of saying the two things a deployed model most needs to do are the two things hardest to do under a fixed clearance.

The data covers one regulatory pathway and its label requirement. It does not say how many plans have been authorized, how the FDA reviews them in practice, or how long authorization takes. It also does not address compute, facilities, or power, and nothing here should be read as a claim about them.

sections.body: Write the change plan with the first submission. Retraining on new data and expanding to new populations are the changes most worth pre-authorizing.
